title: Week of September 12, 2026
description:
BENDY: One chicken cooks itself Thursday and turns into Friday's dinner without me lifting a knife. That's the whole trick this week.

BUB: The chicken works two shifts.

BENDY: Honey sesame chicken Thursday, chopped salad Friday. Same chicken, different shape.

BUB: What do I do today?

BENDY: Today is Saturday, so today is setup. Pull the pork tenderloin and both bags of chicken thighs out of the freezer and into the fridge. Thighs take a full day and a half in there.

BUB: And if we forget?

BENDY: Then Sunday is a sad frozen brick and we order pizza. Also tonight: rub the pork. Kosher salt, rosemary, thyme, garlic, black pepper, straight on the meat, uncovered in the fridge.

BUB: Uncovered? That's weird.

BENDY: Dry surface takes color. A wet tenderloin steams instead of searing and you get gray pork.

BUB: Gross.

BENDY: Then the food processor does the rest. Rice two heads of cauliflower, bag them separately, Monday and Thursday. Chop kale for Wednesday, slice mushrooms for Tuesday. And mix Thursday's sauce now: honey, soy, sesame oil, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger. It keeps in a jar all week.

BUB: Okay. Sunday.

BENDY: Traeger Herb-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Brussels Sprouts and Apples. Smoke at 225 until the middle hits 140, then crank to 450 for four minutes a side.

BUB: Why not just cook it hot?

BENDY: Tenderloin is lean. Hot the whole way and the outside is leather before the center is done. And rest it ten minutes or the juice runs out onto the board.

BUB: What about the sprouts?

BENDY: Halved, cut side down, apples in for the last twelve minutes only. Apples go to mush if they ride the whole time.

BENDY: Monday, Creamy Chicken and Cauliflower Rice Soup, slow cooker. Four hours on low, then the riced cauliflower goes in for the final twenty minutes.

BUB: Twenty? That's nothing.

BENDY: All day and it dissolves. You want little grains you can feel, not soup sludge.

BENDY: Tuesday, Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Zucchini Noodles. Cook the zucchini noodles separately, thirty seconds in a dry hot pan, then drain them.

BUB: Separately? More dishes.

BENDY: Zucchini is basically water. In the sauce it floods the pan and everything turns into soup. Sear the beef in two batches, and slide the mushrooms in after so they brown instead of sweating.

BENDY: Wednesday, Sausage, White Bean and Kale Soup. Brown the sausage first and leave the fat in the pot.

BUB: The fat stays?

BENDY: That fat is the flavor. Onions go into it. Diced butternut squash goes in with the broth so it's tender by the time the kale wilts, and the kale is last, five minutes, or it goes army green.

BENDY: Thursday, Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken with Cauliflower Rice. Cook the thighs dry with the sauce, no extra liquid.

BUB: They won't burn?

BENDY: They release plenty. Add water and the sauce never thickens. Pull a third of the chicken out before dinner and hide it.

BUB: Hide it from who?

BENDY: You. Because Friday is the Honey Sesame Chicken
